articles.title: Cavs' Donovan Mitchell Reacts to Wife Coco Jones Landing 'Hilary' Role in 'Bel-Air' Spin-Off
articles.summary: Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell has his eyes on a new upcoming show.
articles.body:
Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell has his eyes on a new upcoming show.

Which isn't exactly surprising considering his wife, Coco Jones, is going to star in it:

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Nellie Andreeva of Deadline reported Peacock is developing a show titled Hilary , which will be a spin-off of Bel-Air .

"In the proposed spinoff, after accepting an unexpected job offer from celebrity chef Yvonne Durand, Hilary Banks (Jones) impulsively moves to New York determined to prove herself beyond her Bel-Air connections—only to find that success, friendship and love in the city come with a cost she never anticipated," Andreeva wrote.

Bel-Air ran for four seasons and was a reboot of the sitcom The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air , which starred Will Smith.

This news comes after Mitchell and Jones married earlier this month:

Fellow NBA stars Jalen Brunson, Jaylen Brown and Bam Adebayo were all among those in attendance.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry make a major $29.1 million move as retirement rumors continue to swirl
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, has been reeling from an injury plagued season as he spends his time in recovery. Ahead of the new season, .
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, has been reeling from an injury plagued season as he spends his time in recovery. Ahead of the new season, it seems Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have made a multi million dollar move.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry sell their palatial home ahead of the new season raising eyebrows among manyAccording to reports, the Golden State Warriorsâ star player Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha Curry sold their palatial Bay Area mansion at 28 Selby Lane for a whopping $29.1 million.The off market transaction seems to have been made in May as Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry moved out of the affluent town.Earlier in 2021, Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha Curry sold another luxurious property in Atherton for a whopping $31.2 million.For the unversed, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, had bought their recently sold home in 2020 for $30 million. Selling it at $29 million seems like a huge loss for the star player but it has not been made clear what prompted him to make such a move.This 17,761 square feet luxurious home is in Atherton's Redwood Oaks neighborhood which is considered to be one of the richest neighborhoods across the nation.The luxurious home has seven bedrooms, eight and a half bathrooms, separate guest house, walnut orchard, resort-style swimming pool and cabana, a private wine cellar, and expansive indoor living areas.However, neither the Golden State Warriors' star player Stephen Curry nor his wife Ayesha Curry has reacted to the news yet as they remain private about their finances.Is Stephen Curry coming back in the next season to announce his retirement?Ahead of the new season, there have been a lot of speculations about it being the last season for Stephen Curry before he announces his retirement.A few weeks ago, NBA insider Brett Siegel had weighed in on Stephen Curryâs retirement rumors as he said, "In terms of what his future with the Warriors looks like, Curry is not going anywhere anytime soon.âNBA insider Brett Siegel added, "Retirement is obviously on the horizon, but team sources told ClutchPoints that Curry has made it known multiple times throughout the years that he would like to play at least 20 seasons in the NBA. The 2025-26 season was his 17th year."While Stephen Curry has neither confirmed nor denied the rumors, with this being his last season with the Golden State Warriors, many fans remain concerned about his future.At this point in time, the focus remains on Stephen Curryâs recovery as he trains for the next season while he remains out of the spotlight as he spends time with his family.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2027 NBA Draft Big Board with Top 100 Player Rankings
articles.summary: The 2027 NBA draft cycle is officially underway, and unlike the past two classes, there is no clear-cut favorite or consensus superstar sitting atop the board.
articles.body:
The 2027 NBA draft cycle is officially underway, and unlike the past two classes, there is no clear-cut favorite or consensus superstar sitting atop the board.

Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes has emerged as the early favorite for No. 1, but the gap between him and the next tier remains far from definitive.

This is also a class that could change dramatically over the course of the season. A number of returning college players have an opportunity to make significant jumps, while several incoming freshmen are entering college with the size, athleticism and skill sets to quickly establish themselves as NBA prospects.

NIL has also reshaped the draft landscape, keeping more potential first-round talent in college for another season.

With the college and international seasons still ahead, these rankings are a snapshot of the 2027 class based on current evaluation, upside, production, physical tools and NBA projection. Expect plenty of movement as the season unfolds.

Jordan Smith Jr. (Arkansas, PG/SG, 18 years old)

Stefan Joksimovic (Baskonia, SG, 17 years old)

For years, Stokes has been considered the marquee name or face of the projected 2027 draft class. At 6'8", 230 pounds with the ability to initiate offense, score from three levels or provide physicality around the basket, he's the class' safe bet with a body and skill versatility that creates upside.

Worrisome flaws exist for a No. 1 overall candidate, however. There will be a microscope on his shooting consistency and shot selection. His overall decision-making and leadership style have been questioned throughout high school.

At this point before the season, there just isn't another obvious star prospect to take his spot. And Stokes' natural talent remains undeniable, while his projected archetype is definitely valued.

The next batch of prospects have traits that point to surefire NBA players and/or high floors. But they also possess flaws that make it tough to envision high-upside outcomes.

Smith Jr. will earn fans with his athleticism, shotmaking and outstanding defensive intensity. Scouts will also have questions about his size, playmaking and potential to operate as an efficient lead guard.

Holt is very well-rounded now that he's an improved shooter. There's no need to label him with a specific position—Holt should operate as an undersized wing who'll make open threes, move the ball, outmuscle opponents, crash the glass and force turnovers with activity and motor. He just isn't an advanced creator or playmaker, which does raise questions about upside for a 6'5" player.

Joksimovic has crept into the top-five discussion after MVP showings at Eurocamp and the U18 European Championships. He has the positional size, creativity, shotmaking and some vertical pop at the rim. He isn't a high-level facilitator, and there are definitely questions about his defensive outlook for the NBA.

In a wide open draft, Andrews seems to have the ingredients for a draft-board climb with improving perimeter skill that complements a 6'6", 225-pound frame for attacking and finishing. He was the clear standout for Arkansas during its exhibition trip to the Bahamas. His tools and inside-out scoring versatility figure to be a major draw to NBA scouts if he's able to produce consistently at 18 years old. The 2025 Peach Jam MVP has shown he can take over stretches of games with both physicality and shotmaking.

6. Anthony Thompson (Ohio State, SF, 18 years old)

7. Braylon Mullins (Connecticut, SG, 20 years old)

8. Bruce Branch III (BYU, SF, 18 years old)

9. Motiejus Krivas (Arizona, C, 21 years old)

10. Bryson Howard (Duke, SG/SF, 18 years old)

11. Colben Landrew (Connecticut, SG/SF, 18 years old)

12. Amari Allen (Alabama, SG/SF, 20 years old)

13. Patrick Ngongba II (Duke, C, 20 years old)

14. Jason Crowe Jr. (Missouri, SG, 18 years old)

It seems safe to project Mullins in the late lottery group, assuming his shotmaking range and confidence become more productive and dangerous with a greener light. How far he climbs up the board will come down to how much he's added off the dribble, though even the same Mullins as last year should look like a top 15-20 pick.

Branch, Howard and Landrew possess enticing archetypes, but there is some guesswork regarding their roles and readiness. Branch is a three-level scorer with NBA tools. He should have plenty of shots available—the question is whether he's polished enough to efficiently execute as a top option. Howard has the frame, shooting and perimeter self-creation. He just won't have the touches or opportunities to handle the ball. Landrew is listed at 236 pounds and clearly possesses next-level footwork, finishing craft and shotmaking skill. The eye test suggests a surefire pro wing prospect. He could beat out Jayden Ross for minutes if he's consistent enough with his jumper and defensive reads.

Crowe is one of the biggest wildcards of the class. He's the sharpest scorer among freshmen in terms of creation and shotmaking skill, range, feel and the ability to catch fire. His 6'4", 190-pound listing is also encouraging. But NBA teams will want to see some level of playmaking and flashes of rim pressure for them to buy a high-upside outcome, rather than just an offensive spark of instant offense.

Krivas, Ngongba and Allen seem like first-round, high-floor locks after generating first-round interest last year. Ngongba has to stay healthy, however. And teams will want to see Allen take a step forward as an on-ball weapon for Alabama. Krivas just feels extremely safe based on his frame, obvious defensive impact and offensive efficiency in the paint.

15. Dylan Mingo (Baylor, PG, 18 years old)

16. Ivan Kharchenkov (Arizona, SG/SF, 19 years old)

17. Luigi Suigo (Villanova, C, 19 years old)

18. Baba Oladotun (Maryland, SF, 17 years old)

19. Quentin Coleman (Illinois, PG/SG, 18 years old)

20. Brandon McCoy (Michigan, PG/SG, 18 years old)

21. Hugo Yimga-Moukouri (Nanterre 92, SF/PF, 19 years old)

22. Miikka Muurinen (Arkansas, PF/C, 19 years old)

23. Cameron Williams (Duke, C, 18 years old)

24. Najai Hines (Connecticut, C, 19 years old)

25. Abdou Toure (Arkansas, SG/SF, 18 years old)

26. Caleb Gaskins (Miami, SF/PF, 18 years old)

27. Thomas Haugh (Florida, SF/PF, 23 years old)

28. Alijah Arenas (USC, SG, 19 years old)

29. Davis Fogel (Gonzaga, SF, 20 years old)

30. Maximo Adams (North Carolina, SG/SF, 18 years old)

Suigo had teams looking into him as a first-round candidate last May, particularly after he measured 7'3" barefoot, 289 pounds. He's a massive presence inside who registered a 15.0 offensive rebounding percentage and shot 73.0 percent at the rim. There won't be many Big East opponents who can come close to matching Suigo physically. Still, his shooting flashes—18 made threes last year—create the most intrigue and a path toward the lottery.

Even with Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney back at Michigan, McCoy should earn starter minutes and NBA interest with his rim pressure, defensive pressure and secondary playmaking. There are just enough signs of shotmaking potential to anchor McCoy in the first-round discussion.

Since 16 years old, Muurinen has enticed with explosive finishes and perimeter shotmaking for a 7-footer. His obvious physical talent and skill set create a coveted archetype and easy projected fit. Muurinen's decision-making and maturity have just made scouts hesitate. It's also possible critics have over-thought the negatives of a high school teenager.

Williams' talent is easy to identify, but he's likely too raw to play regularly ahead of Ngongba and freshman Joakim Boumtje Boumtje at Duke. Unless Williams looks ahead of the curve as a shooter, he might not have the one-and-done year his recruiting rankings suggest he should.

As a freshman, Hines posted a 16.3 block percentage and 15.3 offensive rebounding percentage at 6'11", 278 pounds. His physicality, activity and defensive presence/instincts will likely be spotlighted and optimized at Connecticut. A strong post game should be enough for NBA teams who'll picture his paint presence and rim protection translating, based on his standout numbers and measurements.

Haugh and Kharchenkov figure to be discussed in first-round conversations all year. At 6'9", Haugh's 58 threes, 41 dunks and a low 9.3 turnover percentage highlight shooting range, athleticism and efficiency for an NBA stretch-4 role. Waiting until the 2027 draft to declare just means dealing with questions about age. With more projected usage, Kharchenkov is a surefire breakout prospect, and his versatility and defensive toughness should make him widely popular, even if the lack of creation and three-point volume raise questions about upside.

Fogel looks like a breakout NBA prospect whose athleticism, shotmaking and passing IQ should pop more in a larger role.

Scouts are hoping to see a more efficient Arenas now that's played 14 games and a healthy offseason. The eye test suggested an NBA-level scorer based on his size, handle, creation ability and shotmaking. The numbers reflect poor execution and shot selection.

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

31. Tyler Tanner (Vanderbilt, PG, 20 years old)

32. Tounde Yessoufou (St. John's, SG/SF, 20 years old)

33. Malach Moreno (Kentucky, C, 19 years old)

34. Arafan Diane (Houston, C, 18 years old)

35. Massamba Diop (Gonzaga, C, 21 years old)

36. Alex Condon (Florida, C, 22 years old)

37. Cameron Houindo (Cedevita, PF, 18 years old)

38. Klark Reithauser (Chalon, SG, 18 years old)

39. Juke Harris (Tennessee, SG/SF, 21 years old)

41. Pryce Sandfort (Nebraska, SF, 22 years old)

42. David Mirkovic (Illinois, PF, 20 years old)

43. Stefan Vaaks (Illinois, SG/SF, 21 years old)

44. Trey McKenney (Michigan, SF, 19 years old)

45 . Matt Able (North Carolina, SG, 19 years old)

Tanner should be one of the faces of college basketball this year. The question is whether he'll change any NBA skeptics' minds about his size and value at the next level. His ability to create advantages offensively with his quickness and dribble is the main draw. Adding to his 167.0 pound frame and three-point volume should be the priorities.

Diane is interesting due to his enormous 7'0", 280-pound frame and passing flashes. Showing defensive discipline could earn him minutes with coach Kelvin Sampson, and minutes should mean strong finishing, rebounding and shot-blocking rates.

Summer foot surgery clouds Mirkovic's season and projection. Getting a late start without proper offseason training could affect his season. A healthy Mirkovic should look like an attractive pro prospect, given his shoot-dribble-pass versatility for a 6'9" rebounding forward.

More winning with Tennessee should help shine more positive light on Harris , whose 21.4 points weren't enough to turn all scouts into buyers. Sarr's athleticism, defensive tools and shotmaking flashes warranted attention last year. But he'll need to look more consistent from deep and threatening off the dribble to solidify first-round interest from around the league.

Moreno's defensive instincts and passing should receive more spotlight in a bigger role. Sandfort should be one of the nation's top shooters with NBA wing size and very diverse shotmaking skill. Vaaks , who had a pair of impressive games for Estonia at this summer's European World Cup Qualifiers, also looks like a breakout prospect with an attractive mix of size, shooting skill and playmaking numbers.

46. Sayon Keita (North Carolina, C, 18 years old)

47. Milan Momcilovic (Kentucky, SF, 21 years old)

48. Flory Bidunga (Louisville, C, 21 years old)

49. Adam Atamna (Ratiopharm Ulm, SG, 18 years old)

50. Roman Domon (Murray State, SF, 20 years old)

51. Nigel James (Marquette, PG, 20 years old)

52. Rueben Chinyelu (Florida, C, 22 years old)

53. Neoklis Avdalas (North Carolina, SG/SF, 20 years old)

54. Billy Richmond III (Arkansas, SG/SF, 20 years old)

55. Moustapha Thiam (Michigan, C, 20 years old)

56. Shelton Henderson (Miami, SG/SF, 19 years old)

57. Paul McNeil (NC State, SG, 20 years old)

58. Johann Grunloh (Virginia, C, 21 years old)

59. Mason Falslev (Utah State, SG, 24 years old)

60. Daniel Jacobsen (Purdue, C, 20 years old)

A pogo-stick big, Keita should generate buzz with his play-finishing and shot-blocking, though the 18-year-old may look too raw to earn serious NBA interest after just one year.

This tier has some potential specialists, including Momcilovic (shooting), McNeil (shooting) and Chinyelu (rim protection).

A lot of offense should run through Avdalas at North Carolina. Big playmaking wings are always in demand, particularly if they're capable from outside. Avdalas did struggle to consistently create clean separation and rim/free-throw attempts, and very low steal and block rates underscore his athletic limitations. He'll need to improve his finishing and three-point percentage to win scouts over.

Richmond will surely be a high-impact player with exciting athleticism, defensive motor and encouraging mid-range scoring flashes. But his stock will be tied closely to his three-point development.

James is small at 6'0", but a powerful frame, explosiveness (14 dunks) and excellent 37.2 assist percentage suggest he's still worth thinking about. Making a jump as a shooter (34.7 percent, 121 attempts) could help James be taken more seriously.

61. Lucas Morillo (Illinois, SF/PF, 18 years old)

62. Dash Daniels (SE Melbourne, PG/SG, 18 years old)

63. JT Toppin (Texas Tech, PF, 21 years old)

64. Joseph Tugler (Houston, PF, 21 years old)

65. Thijs De Ridder (Virginia, PF, 23 years old)

66. Nikolas Khamenia (Connecticut, SF/PF, 19 years old)

67. Arrinten Page (Providence, C, 21 years old)

68. Matas Vokietaitis (Texas, C, 21 years old)

69. Kellen Thames (Saint Louis, SF, 23 years old)

70. Elyjah Freeman (Texas, SF/PF, 21 years old)

71. Nolan Winter (Wisconsin, PF/C, 20 years old)

72. Braden Frager (Nebraska, SF, 19 years old)

73. Jeremy Fears Jr. (Michigan State, PG, 21 years old)

75. Andrej Stojakovic (Illinois, SF, 22 years old)

76. Amani Hansberry (Virginia Tech, PF, 21 years old)

77. John Blackwell (Duke, SG, 21 years old)

78. Zoom Diallo (Kentucky, PG, 20 years old)

79. Finley Bizjack (West Virginia, SG, 21 years old)

80. Alvaro Folguiras (Louisville, PF, 21 years old)

Morillo will generate conversation around his versatility, being a 6'7" wing who operates as a pick-and-roll ball-handler and connective piece. Whether he's able to sell teams on his shooting potential will likely determine if he's viewed as a real NBA prospect.

Daniels will be looking to bounce back with a new NBL team. He started last year in first-round projections. His backcourt versatility and defense have always been draws, but Daniels either needs to improve his creation or shooting.

Frager is a breakout candidate and potential riser if he capitalizes on more usage. He earned a spot on preseason watch lists with his off-ball scoring and shooting skills.

Fears is a strong National Player of the Year candidate and a good bet to lead the nation in assists. NBA teams will want to see more three-point volume for a 6'2", below-average finisher.

Khamenia, Freeman , Diallo and Bizjack all have the chance to benefit from changes of scenery, whether it's due to bigger roles or new teams poised to be more relevant.

81. Ruben Prey (St. John's, C, 21 years old)

82. Paulius Murauskas (Arizona State, PF, 22 years old)

83. Jordan Scott (Michigan State, SF, 19 years old)

84. Miles Byrd (Providence, SG/SF, 21 years old)

85. Amael L'Etang (Dayton, C, 21 years old)

86. Killyan Toure (Iowa State, PG/SG, 20 years old)

87. Tahaad Pettiford (Auburn, PG, 21 years old)

88. Collin Chandler (BYU, SG, 22 years old)

89. Zvonimir Ivisic (Illinois, C, 23 years old)

90. Jalen Haralson (Tennessee, SF/PF, 19 years old)

91. Aiden Sherrell (Indiana, PF/C, 21 years old)

92. Tomislav Ivisic (Illinois, C, 23 years old)

93. Xavier Edmonds (TCU, SF, 22 years old)

95. Bryson Tiller (Missouri, PF, 20 years old)

96. Blue Cain (Georgia, PG/SG, 21 years old)

97. Trent Pierce (Missouri, PF, 21 years old)

98. Coen Carr (Michigan State, SF, 21 years old)

99. Kanon Catchings (Georgia, SF, 21 years old)

100. Teagan Moore (Western Kentucky, SG)

Prey finished last year's season by making four-of-four threes against Duke in the Sweet 16. Turning into a shooting threat with 6'11" size and defensive versatility should earn him spots on NBA watch lists.

Toure's defensive quickness and pressure are so special that even just a capable three-point shot could be enough for him to generate NBA interest.

Pettiford and Byrd had chances at the 2025 first round, but they returned and struggled with their shot and consistency last season. They're bounce-back candidates to track for 2027.

There will be a bigger spotlight on Haralson at Tennessee after his 16.2 points slid below the radar at Notre Dame. He's a big wing who can make plays off the dribble, but for a limited athlete, he'll need to add a three-point shot.

articles.title: Kyle Lowry-Inspired Logo Teased by Raptors in New Video After Star's NBA Retirement
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors hinted at a new potential logo in honor of Kyle Lowry in a social media post on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors hinted at a new potential logo in honor of Kyle Lowry in a social media post on Tuesday.

Lowry, who announced his retirement this offseason after signing a one-day contract with the Raptors, spent nine seasons with the Raptors, averaging 17.5 points and 7.1 assists per game in that time while helping to lead the team to an NBA championship.

The team already announced that his No. 7 jersey would be retired.

"Kyle is the Toronto Raptors—he created an identity for the Raptors that we strive to uphold every time we take the floor, play hard and play to win, for your teammates, for Toronto and for Canada," general manager and executive vice-president Bobby Webster said in a statement after Lowry retired. "Put your body on the line. Take a charge, dive for a loose ball—do all the little things that don't always show up in the box score, but add up to a storied, celebrated career. Kyle was the ultimate competitor whose No. 7 will always be remembered with the Raptors very first championship, and it's our honor to raise it to the rafters, where it belongs."

articles.title: "I'm not competing with anyone": LeBron James breaks silence with a cryptic message as his massive $300 million loan sparks heated debate
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakersâ icon, is preparing for the new season with the Philadelphia 76ers but his finances have raised eyebrows a.
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakersâ icon, is preparing for the new season with the Philadelphia 76ers but his finances have raised eyebrows among fans and experts. In 2018, a private company controlled by LeBron James ended up taking a massive $300 million loan from two Midwestern life insurance companies. This has raised eyebrows and the NBA legend has hinted what his mindset is all about currently.LeBron James hints at what his current priorities are as his massive $30 million sparks a heated debateA few hours ago, the NBA legend LeBron James took to his social to share a post that read as, "I'm not competing with anyone. I don't need to step on people to get ahead and I don't let jealousy distract me from my own path.âThe post added, âI genuinely celebrate other people, stay focused on my own growth and trust that what's meant for me will find me. Life becomes so much lighter when you stop comparing, stop chasing and simply move with peace."While it is not confirmed what LeBron James has been hinting at, the post has raised eyebrows among fans.For now, the news about LeBron James borrowing a whopping $300 million has sparked a heated debate among fans.LeBron Jamesâ loan divides fans and experts over what is âethicalâWhile some fans feel it was a clever move to get away from taxes, others remain concerned about the reason behind taking such a massive loan.A fan took to X and wrote, âHis advisors are f**king brilliant. He can use that $300M to create billions in the next 30 yearsâ¦and heâd only owe the $300M + interest back to the insurers.âAnother fan posted, âSo he did what everybody else in his tax bracket does? Hedge funds use insurance companies like piggy banks.âA third fan wrote, âaverage person realize this is how the wealthy "not pay taxes" they borrow using assets. they dont live on income.âAnother fan posted, âItâs more nuanced than this and hardly a novel observation but one of Americaâs defining truths is that the rich will never, ever, ever pay taxes. They will never let people like us come near it. They have invented schemes for Go Fuck Yourself you couldnât even imagine.âA fifth fan noted, âif you get a loan it isnât taxed correct ? And the future earnings go directly towards to the insurers? They do this same thing with stocks. Goat james.âHowever, neither LeBron James nor his team has issued a statement concerning the speculations about his finances as the NBA legend tries to stay out of the spotlight.For now, all eyes remain on LeBron James and his family as they navigate through this drama.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Olympic hero Nancy Hogshead launches petition calling for WNBA to restrict gender eligibility
articles.summary: Nancy Hogshead's Change.org petition has over 11,000 signatures demanding the WNBA clarify eligibility rules to explicitly include only biological females.
articles.body: Three-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Nancy Hogshead is calling on the WNBA to explicitly restrict player eligibility to biological females. Hogshead recently launched a Change.org petition asking the league to clarify the meaning of "woman" in its eligibility rules. The petition has collected more than 11,000 signatures since its Aug. 14 launch. "We’re calling for the WNBA to clarify that its eligibility rules are for women only," Hogshead told Fox News Digital. "If you wanna participate, you have to be a certain age, and you have to be a female." CHARLES BARKLEY DECLARES WNBA IS 'FOR WOMEN ONLY' AFTER ONGOING TRANSGENDER ATHLETE DEBATE Hogshead said she hopes the petition ultimately reaches 100,000 signatures. "It’s an 80/20 issue across the country, so we can do it," she said. "We have well over a million people who’ve engaged with our materials that we put out about the petition. We just gotta get them to sign on." The WNBA’s 2026 collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." However, the agreement does not further define "woman" or include specific language addressing gender identity or sex assigned at birth. The debate intensified after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while claiming to identify as women. League sources hav since said that neither of them is eligible and characterized their announcements as "publicity stunts." Hogshead said the declarations exposed what she considers a contradiction in policies based on gender self-identification. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT ON PROTECTING GIRLS FROM COMPETING AGAINST 'BIOLOGICAL MEN' "I love it that they came forward because it just shows the hypocrisy of the WNBA, and it shows the hypocrisy of gender ideology," Hogshead said. "For them to come forward and, you know, threaten to play in the WNBA and show up for the draft, it just shows just how ridiculous that gender ideology is." The WNBA previously said there were "no immediate eligibility matters" affecting the league and denounced "bad-faith efforts" to use the debate to "demean or marginalize others." Commissioner Cathy Engelbert also said league officials would continue discussing the subject with the players’ union and other stakeholders. Hogshead’s petition comes amid rallies outside WNBA games supporting Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who publicly opposed transgender participation in girls’ and women’s sports earlier this summer. "I really appreciate her for the stand that she has taken on behalf of women," Hogshead said of Cunningham. "If anything, the more people see of Sophie Cunningham, the more they like her." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hogshead won three gold medals and one silver medal at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. She later became a civil rights attorney and founded Champion Women, an organization that advocates for women and girls in athletics.

articles.title: Georges Niang, Warriors Agree to Contract in NBA Free Agency, Updated Salary Cap and Depth Chart
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors reportedly filled out their roster Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors reportedly filled out their roster Tuesday.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported they agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with Georges Niang. Charania also noted they filled their last two open regular-season roster spots with the additions of Niang and Brandon Williams who "were targeted over the last month for the Warriors and now land on one-year minimum deals."

According to Spotrac , Golden State has $249.4 million in total cap allocations.

Heat still have 2 rosters spot left after signing Klay

Here is a look at the team's potential depth chart :

PG : Stephen Curry, De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton II

SG: Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams, Will Richard

SF: Jimmy Butler (when healthy), Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg

C: Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford, Charles Bassey

Niang surely won't be a go-to option on a roster that includes Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Draymond Green, but he does provide a veteran presence off the bench who can take advantage of openings.

He entered the league as a second-round pick in the 2016 NBA draft and has played for the Indiana Pacers, Utah Jazz, Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers and Atlanta Hawks.

However, the Iowa State product also missed the entire 2025-26 campaign because of a foot injury.

At his best, he is someone who can provide matchup problems for opposing frontcourts because of his outside shooting. Niang is a career 39.9 percent shooter from beyond the arc and connected on 40.6 percent of his triples during the 2024-25 season for the Cavaliers and Hawks on his way to 9.9 points per game.

Given the defensive attention that Curry in particular draws, that should lead to a number of clean looks on the outside for Niang.

His ability to knock them down will ultimately determine how much he plays for a team looking to make a playoff run in the Western Conference.

articles.title: Sky Owner Says Enes Kanter Freedom is Banned From Home Games, Calling Him 'A Potential Threat'
articles.summary: CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever.
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever.

Owner Michael Alter made the announcement in a rare news conference on Tuesday. Alter told reporters Freedom is not allowed inside of Wintrust Arena for Sky games "unless sometime in the future, he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat."

The 6-foot-10, 250-pound Freedom was removed from Sunday's game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.

Enes Kanter Freedom Ejected from WNBA Game

Source: Freedom, White Not Eligible for WNBA Draft (AP)

Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Freedom's direction.

Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Freedom, 34, as she approached him. A standing Freedom held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.

"It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and see how much attention he could get," Alter told reporters from the Chicago Sun-Times and other media outlets.

Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.

He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing the arena.

"I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN!" Freedom wrote on social media. "Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told the AP on Monday that they are not eligible. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

articles.title: Watch Penny Hardaway's motivational speech to Memphis football team
articles.summary: Penny Hardaway spoke to the Memphis football team ahead of the 2026 season. Here's what he told them about what it means to play for the Tigers.
articles.body:
Memphis football coach Charles Huff said at his news conference on Aug. 25 that motivational speeches don't mean much once the game actually starts.

But he also said that after Memphis basketball coach Penny Hardaway delivered an impassioned one to the football team about what it means to play at Memphis.

"We carry the city," Hardaway said in a speech that was posted on social media. "We win, it makes our whole entire city better. The people are more happy. The crime goes down, it's already been documented. So when you have that on you, it should mean something. Whether you care about the city of Memphis or not, it should mean something to you. That pride should mean something."

Hardaway would know. He's a Memphis native who played for the Tigers before going to the NBA, eventually returning to Memphis as head basketball coach. He and Huff have built a strong relationship in the time since Huff was hired in December. He already has visited a football practice and said he plans to be around more during the season.

Memphis football has an entirely new coaching staff and a roster made up mostly of transfers. Huff has talked throughout the offseason about using Hardaway to explain to those players what it means to play for the Tigers.

"I was the No. 1 player in the high school rankings," Hardaway said. "I could've went anywhere in the country. I chose to stay home. I didn't choose to stay home because I was a home guy. I chose it because of how the fans made me feel for sure. And that's the same thing that y'all are going to get. You perform at a high level in this city, they treat you like royalty. The reason why is because this thing goes deeper than just tickets to a game. The city will ride with you as long as you're doing what you're supposed to do."

The football team kicks off its season at UNLV on Aug. 29 (9 p.m. CT, FOX). Memphis basketball's season begins on Nov. 2 against Iowa State in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.

In his speech to the team, Hardaway talked about what it means to play for Tigers fans.

"Y'all have to understand: The days you don't want to get up, the days you don't want to do the extra reps, you've got to push all that to the side because that's nothing compared to what these people have to go through every day," he said. "And spend their money to come and watch y'all play."

Reach sports writer Jonah Dylan at jonah.dylan@commercialappeal.com or on X @thejonahdylan .

articles.title: Klay Thompson drops scary Heat & Giannis Antetokounmpo championship proclamation
articles.summary: Klay Thompson knows that the Heat led by Giannis Antetokounmpo are on the road for an NBA championship run and even he dropped a huge promise.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson drops scary Heat & Giannis Antetokounmpo championship proclamation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Just when everyone thought that the Miami Heat were already scary with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo , they got another daunting acquisition. Klay Thompson decided to join the party in South Beach so that he could get a fifth NBA championship under his belt. How confident is the former Dallas Mavericks and Golden State Warriors sharpshooter that he will be able to play at a championship-level once again? Simply put, he is very certain.

Thompson proclaims big championship-level jump to help Antetokounmpo, Heat

Klay Thompson has been far from his championship-caliber form for a while now. The last time that he was able to score more than 20 points on average in the regular season was during the 2022-23 NBA regular season, a year removed from the Warriors' most recent title run. Since then, he has settled for spot-up shooter roles and taught shooting mechanics to younger players on his squads. Thompson aims to change that with the Heat .

He plans to return to form heading into the 2026-27 NBA season and become the perfect complement to Giannis Antetokounmpo. The veteran sharpshooter declared all of this during his introductory press conference.

"I still think I can do it at a high level. Like you said, the durability has been, for me, a huge plus. You know, that's one thing that might have been questioned from all that time I had off. But, for me, all of those injuries are back in the past. I don't even think about them anymore. It's nice to be able to walk on the floor and play free-minded," Thompson declared.

In his most recent season with the Mavericks, Thompson looked like a shell of his former self. He hit a career-low average of 11.7 points while only knocking down 38.3% of his shots from three-point range. Despite that, he has shown strong durability by playing 69 regular-season games, which Antetokounmpo and the Heat could use in the coming season.

In the bigger picture, this move to acquire Thompson makes a lot of sense. With Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. now off the roster, the Heat need someone who can knock down shots. Schematically, Coach Erik Spoelstra has balanced out their inside and outside scoring. This is why the Heat ranked 10th in the league with their 36.4% field goal percentage. With Antetokounmpo joining the Heat, the need to have an elite spot-up shooter has become more apparent. This is because of the gravity the Greek Freak brings when driving inside the paint.

There is still so much to iron out in terms of rotations along with X's and O's. One thing is certain, however: the Heat need Thompson to equal his production from at least that 2022 Warriors NBA Championship run to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy.

articles.title: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run
articles.summary: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run.
articles.body:
In the final week of August, we're in the dog days of summer. Very little is going on in the NBA world. Most of the offseason homework is done and teams are awaiting training camps to start. Right now, everybody is bored out of their mind. But right around the corner, we're about to see the yearly marathon restart.

The Oklahoma City Thunder enter the 2026-27 season as a co-title favorite — alongside the San Antonio Spurs . Even with their cost-cutting moves this offseason, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren should be enough to keep you in the title hunt.

But with Lu Dort and others out the door, Cason Wallace could be in line for a massive promotion. The 22-year-old will likely become a full-time starter this upcoming season. He'll no longer have to call himself the unofficial sixth starter as he has over the first three seasons of his rich basketball career. He'll also get more opportunities to grow on offense.

With a vacuum of possessions and shot attempts up for grabs, Wallace should see an uptick in offensive production. No longer will he have to settle for catch-and-shoot looks with the occasional downhill drive. Now, OKC's success could depend on his development on that side of the floor. It looks like he's taking it seriously this summer.

Wallace showed off his ball-handling creativity in a recent open gym run. He also showed he can pull up from deep outside. In a social media video that highlighted his best plays, he showed some finesse around his driving game as he kissed the ball off the glass for a layup. Everything is set up for him to be a double-digit scorer for the first time in his career this upcoming season. It's now about running away with that opportunity.

These summer months are when NBA players usually make the most strides in their respective games. The downtime allows them to work on their craft undisturbed. It'll be interesting to see how Wallace looks as he's about to enter his fourth NBA season already.

The Chicago Sky found themselves in the middle of a news cycle involving one of their players and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom.

During the second half of the Sky's 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever , Sky guard Natasha Cloud got into a verbal altercation with Kanter, who was sitting courtside with a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. adult human female." Security at Wintrust Arena then escorted Kanter from the game.

Kanter has since posted on social media and appeared on television defending himself. A new perspective is being told by the owner of the Sky.

Chicago Sky Owner Discusses Enes Kanter Freedom Controversy

Sky owner Michael Alter met with the local media on Tuesday to discuss the incident. According to Front Office Sports' Colin Salao, Kanter's manager texted Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca that Kanter was coming to the game. Alter said that Pagliocca has not talked to Kanter in "three or four years."

After that, Alter made it clear that Kanter's intentions were to be "provocative and just see how much attention he could get," but added he did not know where he was sitting before the game. Alter even spoke to people who were sitting near him to get the story.

"They each confirmed that the dialogue between Cloud and Kanter started with Kanter. He began to chirp with her sometime in the third quarter. I would characterize it as trash talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her." "He portrays as this victimless person who did nothing, said nothing. Just wearing a t-shirt … We have five different security authorities that all agreed very quickly to throw him out because he made himself into a threat."

"They each confirmed that the dialogue between Cloud and Kanter started with Kanter. He began to chirp with her sometime in the third quarter. I would characterize it as trash talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her."

"He portrays as this victimless person who did nothing, said nothing. Just wearing a t-shirt … We have five different security authorities that all agreed very quickly to throw him out because he made himself into a threat."

Alter announced that Kanter will no longer be allowed at Wintrust Arena "unless sometime in the future, he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat." Alter's only regret is that he didn't tell the Sky players before the game, since it was close to tipoff.

Enes Kanter Won't Be Allowed at Chicago Sky Games Moving Forward

This follows conversations about transgender women in sports, first raised by Fever guard Sophie Cunningham . Kanter and other former NBA players joined the conversation by saying they were "declaring" for the 2027 WNBA Draft. The league has since said he and the other players are not eligible.

No other WNBA teams have announced whether they will take action on it. As of the release of this article, Kanter did not respond to the news.

The Chicago Sky are back in action Tuesday to face the Connecticut Sun . They will then face the New York Liberty on Saturday before entering the World Cup break.

articles.title: Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball hires driver following reckless driving incidents in Charlotte, brother Lonzo says
articles.summary: Lonzo Ball revealed that LaMelo Ball has a driver to help with his many road situations after buying $1 million cars and finding ways to damage them.
articles.body: LaMelo Ball’s extensive car collection has drawn attention since his rise to basketball stardom. But the Minnesota Timberwolves guard has now decided to employ a personal driver to help him get around his new NBA home, according to his older brother, Lonzo Ball. During a recent edition of the "Curious Mike" podcast, Lonzo Ball pointed to his younger brother while discussing which member of the Ball family spends the most money with Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. "Who in your family out of y'all three spends the most [money]," Porter asked. "The one who has the most, LaMelo," Lonzo replied. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "[He's] got 10 cars," Lonzo continued. Having a driver could mean the 25-year-old spends less time behind the wheel and, in turn, has fewer opportunities to be involved in an accident. Lonzo also suggested LaMelo could benefit from choosing vehicles outside the exotic-car category, rather than Lamborghinis and similar high-performance models he has owned in the past. LAMELO BALL'S CUSTOM HUMMER LOSES WHEEL IN CHARLOTTE CRASH DURING ALL-STAR BREAK "He'll buy a $1 million car and then just immediately f–k it up, I've never understood [that]," Lonzo added in reference to his sibling's habits when it comes to vehicles. "You just bought that? And then you ripped it up? You could've just got a beater," the former Los Angeles Lakers guard noted. Lonzo then addressed the perception surrounding the frequency of LaMelo’s road incidents, saying his younger brother "doesn’t get into accidents, but he has a lot of situations on the road." The Lakers selected Lonzo Ball with the second overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. He later played for the New Orleans Pelicans and Chicago Bulls before joining the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2025. The Cavaliers traded him to the Utah Jazz in February 2026, but the Jazz subsequently waived him before he appeared in a game for the team. Lonzo's NBA career has been marked by injuries. After appearing in 35 games during the 2021-22 season, he spent more than two calendar years sidelined. "It was like a 1,000 and something days," Ball said, reflecting on the length of his absence. He added that he has come to terms with the possibility that he may not return to the same level he once reached as an athlete. "I came at peace with that when I got hurt the first time. Every time you get hurt it kind of sets you back," Ball told Porter. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Hornets selected LaMelo with the third overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. Charlotte traded the two-time All-Star guard and his teammates Josh Green to the Timberwolves in June for Naz Reid and multiple draft picks.

articles.title: College athletics' latest mess: Court orders say athletes can play, but SEC and Big Ten ready to fight
articles.summary: The SEC and Big Ten voted to bar athletes with pro sports experience, but attorney Ryan Downton says the move violates multiple court orders.
articles.body: The college athletics world is reeling after the SEC and Big Ten created new guidelines governing the eligibility of athletes who planned to join teams this week following injunctions and temporary restraining orders granted by multiple judges. On Tuesday, both conferences, who will soon be joined by the ACC and Big 12, voted to enact new rules that would prevent athletes who have participated in professional sports from reentering the college landscape. The decision comes after players in several states were granted injunctions or temporary restraining orders allowing them to play this season. Most of the lawsuits stem from the NCAA’s new eligibility guidelines, which give athletes five years to play five seasons of college athletics. NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME Conference guidelines prohibit players from NFL, NBA or WNBA Under the new policies, any athlete who has signed with a professional team, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition. But, there was one difference from a public standpoint with the SEC and Big Ten. On Tuesday evening, SEC presidents and chancellors held a vote on how to move forward with the new guidelines pertaining to these ongoing cases revolving around athletes who have participated at the professional level in some form or fashion. NCAA IGNORED THE WARNINGS. NOW IT'S FIGHTING FOR SURVIVAL IN COURTROOMS ACROSS AMERICA OVER ELIGIBILITY In addition to the guidelines created by the SEC, the conference has also given Greg Sankey the power to enforce these rules, which include suspension of coaches and monetary fines to each school who violates them. So, what does this mean for schools who are preparing to bring athletes onto campus for the upcoming college football or basketball season? According to attorney Ryan Downton, who represents a number of players, the are currently "working on a legal strategy" on how to move forward against both the NCAA and participating conferences who have enacted these new guidelines. "The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," Downton told OutKick-Fox News on Tuesday night. "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level" OLE MISS FILES LAWSUITS AGAINST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYERS WHO LEFT FOR LANE KIFFIN'S LSU Multiple sources told OutKick that the vote within the SEC was unanimous, though that does not mean there will not be legal action taken over the next few days. "We are still working on a legal strategy," attorney Ryan Downton noted. Abide by court orders or violate conference guidelines? Decisions upcoming At the forefront of this fight, even though he was not the first coach or team to bring in a player who has in some way competed at the NFL level, is LSU coach Lane Kiffin. Over the last few days, Kiffin has voiced his reasoning behind the recruitment of such athletes who have already gained NFL experience. Essentially, the Tigers coach mentioned that if he didn’t strike first, some other school would. "So, you know, we have you know made a decision to recruit some kids around the country, and through these multiple injunctions around the country, which, this is not a first time in college sports, a group of players were granted a fifth year of eligibility, in multiple sports. And through them winning their injunction and entry into the portal, they’re available to recruit," Kiffin noted on Monday. "So ourselves, like many places around the country, are recruiting them. At the end of the day, you know, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country. So, we made a decision to recruit them, like probably most people are." This includes former Ole Miss football players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who are both set to join the LSU roster thanks to a ruling from the 19th District Court of Louisiana that granted them an additional season of eligibility. But, there have been plenty of others who have gone down this route, winning cases in state courts that allow them to return this season. Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson is another, who sued the NCAA in a Texas court for an additional season. Attorney Darren Heitner, who represents Dae'Quan Wright, told OutKick that the SEC should abide by the order granted by the 19th District Court of Louisiana. "He should be rostered by LSU and be a great contributor for the Tigers. The SEC should heed the court order recently issued by a Louisiana judge," Heitner said. The question is whether LSU, and others, will move forward in bringing in athletes knowing that it would be in violation of conference rules, but also legal in the eyes of the courts who have granted them injunctions. articles.title: Updated 2026 WNBA Playoffs Bracket Picture and Standings After Paige Bueckers, Wings Clinch Berth
articles.summary: The Dallas Wings are heading to the WNBA playoffs for the first time since 2023.
articles.body:
The Dallas Wings are heading to the WNBA playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Dallas clinched a spot in the 2026 postseason Tuesday with a 96-78 win over the Portland Fire. The Wings clinched the final playoff spot, meaning the Fire have been eliminated from postseason contention.

Now that the Wings are officially in, their attention will turn toward the battle for seeding. They are currently in eighth place in the WNBA standings and playoff picture

The eighth seed will play the first seed in the first round of the WNBA playoff bracket, meaning Dallas could be in store for a showdown against the Minnesota Lynx if the current playoff position holds.

Dallas making the playoffs represents one of the most impressive turnarounds in recent league history, as it was an ugly 10-34 last season and 9-31 during the 2024 campaign. It ended up with the first overall pick of the 2025 and 2026 WNBA drafts, and it turned to UConn's backcourt each time as it built the foundation for a contender.

Paige Bueckers wasted little time establishing herself as one of the WNBA's biggest stars after the Wings took her with the first pick in 2025. She captured the Rookie of the Year and was an All-WNBA Second Team selection as a bright spot for a struggling club.

Dallas then gave her a familiar teammate when it selected Azzi Fudd with the first pick in this year's draft. While Fudd hasn't been quite as dominant as Bueckers, she provided immediate shooting on the wing and remains one of the best in the league from long distance.

Playing alongside Bueckers certainly makes life easier for her and the rest of the Wings, as the guard draws plenty of defensive attention and creates openings for all of her teammates. She was once again an All-Star in her second season and has taken a leap to become an even more dominant playmaker.

In fact, she has remained in MVP discussions for much of the season, and an All-WNBA First Team selection would be anything but a surprise.

While Bueckers has been the driving force behind Dallas' turnaround with Fudd providing important secondary contributions, it hasn't all been about the youth movement.

Veterans Arike Ogunbowale and Jessica Shepard have made their presence felt with leadership and much-needed offense. They are each averaging better than 14 points a night, while Shepard is a double-double threat every time she steps on the floor.

Her inside presence provides balance and offensive versatility, which helps the Wings make opponents pay when they focus too much on the perimeter with Bueckers and the wing with Ogunbowale.

The Wings may be a season or two ahead of schedule with such a dramatic turnaround, but they are a threat to anyone in the playoffs with a superstar like Bueckers who can take over at a moment's notice and a solid supporting cast in place.

That single line drew the hardest boundary of the whole saga: not a suspension, not a warning, but an outright ban from the building.The trouble started late in the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever. Freedom was sitting baseline in a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. adult human female."Cloud, fresh off a bucket and a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly, walked straight at him, yelling and pointing. Freedom stood, held his arms out, and stepped onto the court before security and several Sky players moved between them. Nobody threw a punch. Security still walked him out.On his way through the lobby, Freedom spun around, held his shirt out toward the crowd, and talked to a group of police officers before he left the building. He later posted on social media that he'd been "kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN."The league itself had reportedly planned to let the incident pass without punishment, since Freedom never actually stepped onto the playing surface. Alter clearly saw it differently. Freedom and fellow former NBA player Royce White have both declared for the WNBA draft on the same grounds, though a person familiar with the league's thinking told the AP that neither is considered eligible. The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement restricts the league to women but stops short of defining gender identity or sex assigned at birth, which is exactly the loophole both men say they're testing.Chicago Sky arena ban sparks intense reactionSocial media did what social media does. A few pushed back on the framing entirely, insisting "she wasn't the one who started it" and demanding people "let her play."Stephen A. Smith responds to Enes Kanter Freedom's campaignStephen A. Smith weighed in with his usual mix of sympathy and scolding. He credited Freedom's history of standing up to the Turkish government but said stepping toward Cloud was "excessive," adding that the WNBA players themselves "don't deserve" to be caught in the middle of a fight that belongs with the league, not the roster.âIt was a classless thing for him to do because it's not the ladies that are playing don't have anything to do with this. The league does. It's collective bargaining agreement may be the case. The liberal tilt that it has might be a cause or a cause effect to some degree. I get all of that,â Smith shared.He added, âBut the actual ladies that are involved, they have nothing to do with this and they don't deserve to be agitated the way he clearly was willing to do in attendance at the game.âFreedom hasn't backed off. If anything, the ban gives him one more grievance to fold into a draft campaign that was already built on confrontation. articles.summary: NBA News: Charles Barkley does not hesitate to tiptoe around a topic, and recently, the WNBA's roughest stretch of the season gave him plenty to swing at. Talki.
articles.body: Charles Barkley does not hesitate to tiptoe around a topic, and recently, the WNBA's roughest stretch of the season gave him plenty to swing at. Talking through the league's ugliest recent headlines, the Hall of Famer landed on a claim that had nothing to do with basketball skill and everything to do with why two of the league's biggest names keep drawing so much heat from their peers.The comments came on The Michael Smerconish Program, where Barkley and the host spent time picking apart what Barkley called the WNBA's "awful year." Barkleyâs comment stems from DiJonai Carrington's hard foul on Sophie Cunningham.Charles Barkley drops unexpected take on Caitlin Clark and Sophie CunninghamThe foul itself happened on Aug. 8, when DiJonai Carrington caught Sophie Cunningham in the head during a fast break, leaving her with a bloody mouth. Officials reviewed it and upgraded the call to a Flagrant 2, ejecting Carrington from the game.What turned a rough basketball play into a national story was what came next. Carrington posted "WHITE PRIVILEGE" on social media shortly after, tagging the Fever, then later said she never meant the foul itself was about race without clarifying what she did mean.Barkley wasn't interested in overthinking the play. "A dirty play. Period," he said, brushing aside any attempt to complicate what he saw as a simple hard foul. He argued Carrington's post, not the contact, is what dragged race into a conversation that started on the court."When you turn stuff to the internet, all the race hustlers start coming out. We have a ton of race hustlers out there, White and Black. Let me repeat that. White and Black," Barkley said.Charles Barkley explains why he thinks WNBA stars hate Caitlin Clark and Sophie CunninghamBarkley stopped short of calling anyone in the league racist, saying flatly he had no proof for that kind of claim. But he didn't shy away from a theory of his own for why Clark and Cunningham draw so much friction from other players. He pointed to a mix of factors rather than one single cause, saying he couldn't begin to sort out how much each one mattered."Those girls do not like Caitlin Clark or Sophie Cunningham. Without regard for race, they just donât like them," Barkley shared."Sheâs just a really good basketball player. Same thing with Sophie. Sheâs a good player. I think it has something to do with se*uality, race, and jealousy. I think itâs all three of them. I donât know how you break up the percentages."The league is growing, players are earning more under a new labor deal, and there's a wave of young talent that should be the story. Instead, he said, the headlines keep circling back to hard fouls and social media fights instead of the games themselves. âI donât think it works like that anymore, Michael. Whenâs the last time you heard something positive about the WNBA? I canât even remember."Colin Cowherd compares Caitlin Clark to Michael Jordan and Stephen CurryWhile Barkley was dissecting the WNBA's off-court drama, Colin Cowherd was busy handing out one of the boldest comparisons Clark has received all year. On "The Herd," Cowherd described her as a blend of two of basketball's most decorated names, pointing to her refusal to engage with any of the noise surrounding her as proof of a Jordan-like mindset layered onto Curry-level scoring range.Cowherd backed the praise with numbers, noting Clark's status among the league leaders in assists and scoring while running what he called the best offense in WNBA history. Clark is averaging 22.1 points, 8.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds a game this season, numbers that have kept her firmly in the MVP conversation as Indiana heads toward the playoffs. The Fever's next test comes at home against the Sun on Aug. 28.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: RJ Luis Jr. cleared by judge to play for LSU after spending time with 2 NBA teams
articles.summary: Former St. John’s standout RJ Luis Jr. has been cleared by a court to start practicing with LSU and potentially play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season.

Luis, who briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics but never played in an NBA game, hugged LSU coach Will Wade after the ruling by East Baton Rouge Parish District Court judge Ronald R. Johnson.

After a five-hour hearing, Johnson granted the player's request for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which had argued Luis was unlikely to win reinstatement after leaving college to turn pro in 2025.

"This is precedent. It's monumental," said Baton Rouge-based attorney Tony Clayton, who represented Luis along with Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina. "This allows him to go practice, go play and we'll let the legal process work itself out."

The timeline for that process was not immediately clear.

"I don't know, but there's a lot of discovery that Elliot and I have to obtain," Clayton said. "We've got a lot of questions."

Luis' attorneys noted that the NCAA had granted exceptions allowing numerous players from overseas professional leagues to join college basketball programs, and argued that American players must be afforded the same opportunity.

They stressed that Luis not only had never played in an NBA game, but also had not played for the Celtics' G League affiliate because of an injury, and had far less of a professional basketball resume than numerous college players who'd been recruited from abroad.

NCAA attorney Taylor Askew argued that Luis' situation was not comparable to those who played for the developmental squads of pro organizations overseas because Luis chose to leave college for the NBA.

Askew noted that the only player in a similar situation to Luis was Alabama's Charles Bediako, who won a temporary retraining order allowing him to play five games for Alabama last season before an Alabama judge ultimately sided with NCAA assertions that he was ineligible.

"I understand Mr. Luis is disappointed that he was not drafted and did not play in the NBA as much as he would have liked," Askew said. "Actions have consequences. Decisions have outcomes and they're not always the right ones or the ones that you want."

As he made his ruling, Johnson said, "In the court's mind, (Luis) did not actually play professional basketball," and that whether Luis was properly advised of his options at the time he left college "lingers heavily before this court."

articles.title: Michigan State basketball center Anton Bonke joins Dutch National Team
articles.summary: A key member of the 2026-27 MSU basketball team is set to get some important experience in the World Cup Qualifiers
articles.body:
One extremely important member of the 2026-27 Michigan State basketball team is about to get some invaluable experience at the international level. Anton Bonke , the Spartans' new center who transferred to the program from Charlotte, will join the Dutch National Team heading into the World Cup Qualifiers. Bonke was born in the Netherlands.

Bonke started his collegiate career at Providence before transferring to Charlotte. At 7-foot-2 with some ability to space the floor, Bonke is an intriguing prospect, so you can be sure that NBA and EuroLeague scouts will be watching Bonke closely as he gets to play some high-level competition abroad.

The Netherlands next play on Thursday against Germany and they play Croatia on Sunday. Bonke averaged 10.6 points and 8.3 rebounds per game last year for Charlotte and hit 34.2 percent of his threes.
